signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ + Intervention
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 160.55, testing the 160.00 psychological barrier as markets await the Bank of Japan policy announcement. The pair anchors a dominant G10 theme where the JPY has outperformed the G10 basket by +1.083% over the last week while the USD has lagged by -1.230%, creating a significant 2.312% spread. Despite recent intervention speculation that drove price below 158.00, the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage continues to attract buyers on dips. Options markets signal caution with a -1.38 moderate put skew in 25d risk reversals, while retail traders remain 82% short, a contrarian signal for further upside. JPY COT LF net short of -114,030 confirms a crowded short position vulnerable to any hawkish BoJ surprise. Risk: A hawkish BoJ shift or formal intervention forces a rapid unwind of carry positions toward the SMA200 at 157.93.

signals.title: AUD/USD — PPI Surprise + ESI Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD holds at 0.7023, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster following a hotter-than-expected Australia Q2 PPI print of +3.6%. This inflation beat contrasts with a broadly negative Economic Surprise Index (ESI) for AUD at -16.7, suggesting that while general data has disappointed, price pressures remain sticky. The 70bp AUD carry premium over USD (OIS basis) supports the pair while the Fed remains on hold. Speculative positioning remains net long (+20,521), but the options market shows a -0.72 put skew, and the 5.5% Vol Risk Premium indicates high hedging demand for downside protection. The pair is caught between a hawkish RBA bias and a widening US-Iran conflict that typically favors USD safe-haven flows. Risk: Escalation in Middle East tensions triggers a broad risk-off move that overrides the AUD carry advantage.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Geopolitical Risk + Volatility Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD softens to 1.1518 as headlines regarding the widening US-Iran conflict provide a safe-haven bid to the USD. The pair is currently trading above its SMA20 (1.1424) and SMA50 (1.1487) but remains capped below the SMA200 at 1.1635. While the ECB-Fed nominal spread is 135bp in favor of the USD, the real rate differential is narrower at 139bp given lower Eurozone inflation expectations. COT data shows a heavy net short spec position for EUR (-80,570), suggesting the market is already positioned for downside, yet the +2.7% Vol Risk Premium confirms that traders are still paying up for put protection. This high VRP suggests the market is not complacent about geopolitical headlines. Risk: De-escalation of conflict leads to a short-squeeze in the crowded EUR spec position back toward 1.1600.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Outperformance + Technical Anchor
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5871, supported by a strong bounce in consumer confidence to 99.3 and a high-performing Economic Surprise Index (+30.6). Despite the RBNZ's accommodative real rate of -1.56%, the currency has outperformed peers this week with a +0.531% G10 average. NZD/USD is technically constructive, holding a position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5786-0.5825), which now acts as a firm support zone. Speculative positioning is significantly net short at -31,649 (long% only 12.0%), which appears increasingly disconnected from the positive domestic data trend. This positioning extreme creates an asymmetric risk profile where any further positive NZD data is likely to trigger a violent short covering rally. Risk: Rising oil prices at $81.8 weigh on NZD consumer sentiment and invalidate the domestic recovery thesis.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Correlation Break + Carry Advantage
signals.text: USD/CAD is at 1.4014, exhibiting a notable correlation break with WTI Oil (corr -0.906 vs norm +0.013, z=-1.51σ). Typically, CAD tracks oil prices, but the current regime sees the pair dominated by the 150bp USD carry advantage and broader USD strength. The pair is trading below its SMA20/50 cluster (1.4105/1.4046), suggesting a loss of short-term bullish momentum despite the favorable rate differential. CAD speculative positioning is deeply short (-99,823), reflecting a lack of confidence in the Loonie despite neutral domestic economic surprises. This decoupling from oil suggests that CAD is being used more as a funding currency than a commodity play in the current environment. Risk: A sustained rally in WTI Oil above $85 forcing a re-convergence of the historical correlation and a drop in USD/CAD.
